thread:
kevin: Heads up — received an EU deletion request for account EU-778. Customer insists on deletion proof including backups. Forwarding PDF to legal.
zhang: thanks. Quick Q: were any backups encrypted with a customer-managed key that we rotated last year? that affects our ability to produce cryptographic proof.
kevin: inventory looks like: 1) primary snapshot eu-north1 snap-778-a, 2) archive eu-west snap-778-arch-2024, 3) offsite `vaultline` export 2024-08. Archive references KMS key `projects/redwood/keys/cust-eu-778` v1->v2.
ops: I can run a key-state check. note: there was a temporary IAM grant to `backup-service@redwood` in 2025-12 for restore testing; it was revoked after 6 hours. Could be relevant.
legal: please attach the DSAR PDF. For EU we either provide verifiable deletion or a documented refusal. If proof is impossible due to technical reasons, we need an auditable narrative plus KMS logs.
zhang: plan suggestion: (A) validate object existence + hashes (B) check KMS key versions + HSM destruction events (C) request short-lived decrypt rights if needed (D) run embedding index sweep for EU-778 and mark candidate artifacts.
kevin: agreed. Also flag: there was a small vulnerability ticket (VULN-2026-78) last month where a service account temporarily got broader KMS roles during a rollout. That might create a window where blobs were re-encrypted. We need to include the vuln triage notes in chain-of-custody.
sre: can confirm VULN-2026-78 timeline. mitigations applied 2026-02-02. I'll attach the triage doc.
ops: for (C) we should use a breakglass CR with minimal scope. I propose: `CR-BG-2026-88`, grant `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` to `dsar-audit@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for 2 hours. Log all actions to immutable export.
zhang: good. Also request that the decrypt attempts run in a sealed environment where output is written to a dedicated GCS bucket `gs://dsar-eu-778-evidence` with object-level checksums and signed manifests.
kevin: include GPG-signed manifest and hash of signed manifest. privacy-bot: Automated note — attach DSAR ID EU-778-2026 and mark high-priority.
legal: please include privacy@legal. Also, if offsite provider `vaultline` holds exports, we need a deletion API call and a letter from them confirming wipe. include timeline for that interaction.
ops: I'll open CR-BG-2026-88 with ops+infra approvers and set TTL 2h. Will run a pre-check to confirm service account has no other privileges. Example command in CR:
```
# grant temporary decrypt role
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding cust-eu-778 --member=serviceAccount:dsar-audit@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
# after tests revoke
```
zhang: remember to capture `cloudkms` audit logs showing keyVersion access and any `decrypt` RPCs. export to `bigquery.audit_dsar` and snapshot that table into the evidence bucket.
kevin: embeddings note — run this SQL to find derived items:
```
SELECT id FROM embeddings WHERE account_tag='EU-778' LIMIT 10000;
```
and produce a deletion plan for both primary and read-replicas.
sre: I'll coordinate replica purge window to avoid breaking analytics jobs. suggest marking rows as tombstoned and then async vacuum after confirmation.
legal: if we cannot decrypt certain archives because of destroyed key versions, we will need KMS key lifecycle logs showing destroy events. That can be used as evidence of irrecoverability. Do not attempt to claim deletion without solid logs.
kevin: timeline: ops to open CR today, run inventory and key verification within 24h, attempt decrypt tests within 48h, reach out to `vaultline` support for offsite deletion concurrently. I'll draft an interim response to the requester indicating steps and expected timeline.
ops: CR-BG-2026-88 opened: https://cr.redwood.internal/CR-BG-2026-88. Change window 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC. ops and infra signed.
zhang: I'll run the key-version audit and export logs to `bigquery.audit_dsar`. Will also run a checksum export of matching objects and place them in `gs://dsar-eu-778-evidence/checksums/`.
kevin: once decrypt+deletion actions complete, collect signed manifests from storage, KMS logs, CR history, and vuln-triage doc into the evidence bundle. Legal will review before sending proof to customer.
legal: noted. keep all communication internal until legal signs off. If we need to refuse, we will use standard refusal template.
kevin: thanks everyone. tagging @zhang @ops @legal @sre. I'll update DSAR tracker after tests. :white_check_mark:
